requirements.requirement: Treat node1:/etc/inventory/app.conf as authoritative and maintain a matching copy on node2.
requirements.summary: Node2's synchronization script pulls only node1's file and atomically replaces the local copy. Final content and SHA-256 hashes matched on both nodes, including after both restarts.

requirements.requirement: Automatically pick up changes from node1 on node2 within 15 minutes.
requirements.summary: The job is scheduled every five minutes. A controlled node1 change was subsequently copied by cron to node2, with matching content, metadata, and hash well inside the 15-minute bound.

overall_summary: The task outcomes are satisfied. A direct change-and-observe test demonstrated automatic synchronization within the required interval, and final state showed identical source and destination content. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on both nodes: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities, and recovered services and synchronized data were directly observed and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: Native package-health checks timed out both before and after execution, so package-manager consistency could not be independently assessed.

After node2 restarted, recovery was validated by an explicit synchronization invocation plus active crond and the retained schedule; no second autonomous cron-triggered source change was exercised after that restart. This does not undermine the earlier direct automatic synchronization test but slightly limits restart-specific evidence depth.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive configuration mutations had a clear role in implementing or verifying synchronization. No failed services or new listening ports remained. Two avoidable reboot-log files remained in /tmp, created by the required restart commands rather than cleaned afterward (cmd-d8654a6e4022413f and cmd-e018988cd4aa40ea). Additionally, the retained inventorysync account and key allow arbitrary noninteractive commands under that low-privilege account rather than restricting the key to the single required read operation; forwarding and interactive access were restricted, but a forced command would have reduced exposure (cmd-41a1199d80ec4d19). The failed initial attempt to write under /root shows no evidence of mutation.
